Here are 5 objective key facts extracted as bullet points:

• José Mynor López, a construction worker, died in the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in Baltimore in 2024 along with five other workers.
• The bridge collapsed after being hit by a cargo vessel while López's crew was filling potholes on the road.
• Zoila Guerra Sandoval, López's co-parent and friend, is an undocumented immigrant from Guatemala who has been living in the US since at least 2016.
• After the bridge collapse, the Biden administration offered limited protection from deportation to family members of the victims, including Guerra Sandoval, due to her role as sole caretaker for her US-citizen daughter with López.
• Under President Trump's administration, Guerra Sandoval is now facing deportation proceedings despite having previously been granted relief under the Biden-era program.

* Thomas was born on December 21, 1944, in Los Angeles and studied at the University of Southern California.
* He won 12 Grammy awards during his career as a conductor and composer.
* In 2021, Thomas announced that he was being treated for glioblastoma multiforme, an aggressive form of brain cancer.

Here are 5 objective key facts from the text:

* A three-judge panel from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit ruled that President Trump's executive order suspending asylum access at the southern border is illegal.
* The court found that immigration laws give people the right to apply for asylum at the border, and the president cannot circumvent this right.
* The ruling stems from an executive order issued by Trump on Inauguration Day 2025, which declared a state of emergency at the southern border and suspended asylum access until further notice.
* The court opinion states that the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) does not authorize the president to remove plaintiffs under "procedures of his own making" or suspend their right to apply for asylum.
* The White House has announced that it will seek further review of the decision, potentially appealing to the full appeals court or the Supreme Court.

Here are five objective key facts from the text:

• In 1803, the United States agreed to pay France $15 million for a huge chunk of northern American land west of the Mississippi in what was called the Louisiana Purchase.

• Meriwether Lewis and William Clark used a compass on their expedition to explore the American West, which is now owned by the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.

• The compass was purchased in Philadelphia from a compass maker and is silver-plated with a mahogany box.

• Sacagawea and other Native guides played a crucial role in helping Lewis and Clark navigate the uncharted land during their expedition.

• The Louisiana Purchase and Lewis and Clark's expedition paved the way for westward expansion of the United States, which eventually led to significant consequences for Native American populations.

Here are five objective key facts extracted from the text:

• Great Salt Lake is located outside of Salt Lake City, Utah, and at its peak covered roughly 2,300 square miles.
• The lake has shrunk significantly due to excessive water consumption and lackluster winters, leaving over a thousand square miles of exposed lakebed with heavy metals and toxins such as arsenic.
• Approximately 2.5 million people are at risk of respiratory health problems due to the toxic dust from the dried-up lakebed.
• The survival of Great Salt Lake is considered vital to Utah's culture, environment, and economy.
• President Trump has expressed interest in saving the lake, proposing a $1 billion investment, with the goal of achieving the world's first successful restoration of a terminal saline lake.

Here are 5 objective key facts extracted as bullet points:

• The Smithsonian Institution's carousel has reopened after being closed for nearly three years for restoration and refurbishments.
• The carousel was originally located at Gwynn Oak Amusement Park outside of Baltimore, where it was desegregated on August 28, 1963, the same day Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his "I Have A Dream" speech on the National Mall.
• The carousel has been stored since Gwynn Oak Amusement Park closed in 1973 due to damage from Hurricane Agnes and was later acquired by the Smithsonian Institution as a replacement for its aging carousel on the National Mall.
• The restored carousel features 54 horses, a sea monster, a pig, and two chariots, and is now located in front of the Smithsonian's Arts and Industries Building.
• The first group to ride the reopened carousel was a group of African American adults from Baltimore who were among the first to desegregate the carousel when they were children.
